title: Latency + Cost Tradeoffs Framework for Platform Buyers
body:
Purpose:
- Quick reference for sales/solutions teams when customers ask: 'Which tradeoffs do we make if we go with a hyperscaler managed endpoint vs Redwood? Where do we save money vs where do we pay premium?'
- Give concise, technical-first talking points, an ops-friendly decision matrix, and rebuttals for common vendor sales traps.

Audience / buyer personas:
- Platform engineering (primary): cares about latency SLOs, predictable tail-latency, autoscaling behavior, and integration with existing infra (IAM, VPCs).
- Product engineering / infra architects: cares about per-call cost, developer ergonomics, SDK & rollout support.
- Finance / procurement (secondary): wants unit economics, committed spend vs usage-based.

High-level thesis (one-liner):
- Hyperscaler managed endpoints simplify model hosting but often push hard on flexibility and convenience while trading off per-unit economics, tail latency, and deterministic fallbacks — Redwood's message: we give you hyperscaler convenience with predictable, cost-optimized inference at scale and ops controls to avoid surprise bills.

Decision dimensions (how buyers actually reason):
1) Latency (p50/p95/p99) and variance
   - Hyperscalers: generally decent p50, but variable p95/p99 due to multi-tenant cold starts, instance spin-up, and opaque routing.
   - Redwood: continuous batching + KV/prefix caching + warm pools reduce p95/p99 variance; dedicated pools for fixed SLOs.
2) Cost-per-token and unit economics
   - Hyperscalers: simple per-invocation + instance-hour math, but opaque queuing + autoscaling can spike costs; little built-in batching heuristics.
   - Redwood: smart batching, quantization recommendations, and model-fallback routing reduce tokens/compute; show measurable 20-60% unit cost reductions in typical production workloads.
3) Reliability & graceful degradation
   - Hyperscalers: rely on multi-region infra; failover is coarse and model downgrades are manual.
   - Redwood: automated model variant fallbacks, tiered capacity routing, and on-platform rollbacks tailored to inference workloads.
4) Security / compliance / networking
   - Hyperscalers: native cloud controls + marketplace contracts; good for cloud-first customers.
   - Redwood: private deployment (VPC/on-prem) option + KMS/HSM integrations for regulated workloads.
5) Developer experience & integration
   - Hyperscalers: single cloud SDKs, infra familiarity is a plus.
   - Redwood: unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, first-class SDKs, dev templates for common patterns (chat, rerank, embeddings), faster local-to-prod parity.

Ops-friendly decision matrix (quick read):
- If your priority is lowest possible engineering lift and you are OK with variable per-unit economics -> hyperscaler managed endpoint.
- If your priority is predictable p99 latency, low unit cost at production scale, and fine-grained ops controls -> Redwood Dedicated or Private.
- If you need hard compliance (air-gapped / HSM) and want consistent tooling across environments -> Redwood Private.

Field hooks (short soundbites for SDR/AE/SE):
- "Pay for inference you actually use, not for hidden queue wait and cold starts."
- "Keep call latency predictable at p99 — we tune batching and cache policies to your workload, not ours."
- "Single API for hosted, dedicated, and private means rollouts are the same whether you run in our cloud or your VPC."

Common buyer objections and rebuttals (tech-forward):
- Objection: 'We already use SageMaker/Vertex/Managed AI endpoints, switching is risky.'
  - Rebuttal: 'We do migration blueprints — start with a canary route to Redwood Dedicated and route 1-5% traffic. Our SDK and model-variant mapping means the app code changes <5% of the time. We also provide traffic shaping to compare cost/latency side-by-side.'
- Objection: 'Hyperscalers give us consolidation onto existing billing and IAM.'
  - Rebuttal: 'Consolidation is valuable — Redwood integrates with cloud IAM and billing connectors and can live in your VPC. The question is whether consolidation of billing is worth a 30–50% higher unit cost or unpredictable tail latency.'
- Objection: 'We don’t trust third-party inference for PII.'
  - Rebuttal: 'Redwood Private runs in your environment with KMS/HSM; we can adopt your audit policies and retention windows.'

Quantitative anecdotes to use (field-ready):
- Example A (consumer-facing chat): 'By enabling streaming + prefix caching we reduced median token compute by ~18% and p99 latency by 36ms vs a baseline managed endpoint test.'
- Example B (high-throughput embedding pipeline): 'Batching + quantization cut GPU-hours by ~40% for production embedding refreshes in one customer POC.'

Technical appendix (for SEs):
- Why p99 matters: tail latency dominates UX for chat/real-time features; per-request queuing that hyperscalers don't expose can cause 2–5x p99 variance on bursty traffic.
- What we tune: batching window heuristics, token-aware batching, KV/prefix cache TTLs, cold-start pre-warms, kernel selection for quantized models, autoscaling cooldowns.
- Quick migration steps: 1) mirror traffic via canary route; 2) measure p50/p95/p99 + cost per token; 3) enable batching/kv caching on Redwood with same model weights; 4) iterate quantization suggestions; 5) flip route once SLOs and cost targets met.

Sales collateral checklist (what to attach to an AE outreach):
- Short one-pager: 'Redwood vs Hyperscaler: Latency & Cost tradeoffs' (recommended)
- Appendix: canned benchmark results for common model families and sequence lengths
- Migration checklist + sample k8s-free on-prem deployment spec

Open questions / experiments to run (internal ops & research):
- Establish a set of 5 canonical benchmarks (chat 1:1 small, chat group, embeddings at batch sizes 128/1024, completion 2k tokens, reranking) and run monthly vs major hyperscaler managed endpoints to keep PRs honest.
- Capture a library of customer-specific workload profiles so we can map expected unit-cost savings per vertical (e.g., enterprise search vs consumer chat).

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Share with SEs and ask for 3 real customer objections we've seen in last quarter; convert those into rebuttal lines.
- Draft one-pager and get marketing to produce a bounded benchmark visualization (p99 vs $/k tokens) for sales playbook.

— end —
